name: Creality Falcon2 Pro 22W
tagline: 22W High-power diode with built-in air assist and color engraving gimmick
tldr: The 22W version of Creality's enclosed Falcon2 Pro: a Class 1 cabinet with air assist that engraves wood and leather cleanly and cuts thin plywood. The sensible entry point to an enclosed diode if you do not need fast thick cuts.

priceRange.note: Official Creality store, Oct 2026: $899 to $1,599 depending on kit and 2W IR option

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Class 1 enclosure with 360° see-through panels: no goggles in normal use
10 mm basswood in one pass, per Creality
Cheapest way into the Falcon2 Pro ($899 single unit, October 2026)
cons: Slow fills at this power: about 17–26 min for a 10 × 10 cm photo in our benchmark
No fine-detail second module in the box at this tier
The enclosure takes more room than an open frame: plan a dedicated table
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 22W SKU on Creality Falcon2 Pro. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Tune cut passes with air assist and focus checks. For photo engraving, slow down vs your cut presets: this head is optimized for throughput on wood, not only finesse.
primaryUse: Cut-biased diode tier for makers who outgrew 10–20W job times but stay on the same frame
mainObjective: Faster cutting and deeper hobby cuts while keeping solid engraving capability

editorialDepth.advantages: Creality Falcon2 Pro 22W targets mixed engraving and wood-cutting weeks: fewer passes on basswood and dark acrylic than weaker SKUs in the same line.
editorialDepth.limitations: Wrong pick if you never engrave and only wanted the lowest price. Ultra-fine photo work can look better on an engraving-first SKU. Open-frame: safety and smoke are on you.

faq.question: How thick can the Falcon2 Pro 22W cut?
faq.answer: Creality's European site rates the 22W module at 10 mm basswood in one pass; some resellers quote 15 mm, which we treat as optimistic. Our benchmark took about 9–14 min for a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood, and dark acrylic up to about 5 mm works.

faq.question: Falcon2 Pro 22W or 40W?
faq.answer: The 22W single unit was $899 on Creality's store in October 2026, the 40W (sold with a 1.6W fine-detail module) $1,349: $450 more. Take the 22W for engraving and occasional cuts up to 6 mm; take the 40W if you cut plywood or dark acrylic every week.

faq.question: What does the Pro enclosure change compared with the open Falcon2?
faq.answer: The Falcon2 Pro is a Class 1 enclosed machine with see-through panels, so it runs without goggles in normal use and contains smoke for extraction. That costs about $300 more than the open Falcon2 22W ($899 single unit against $589 for the Falcon2 22W Basic Kit, October 2026).

standoutFeatures.title: Enclosed and visible
standoutFeatures.body: Class 1 certification with 360° see-through panels: you watch the job without goggles, and smoke stays inside for the exhaust.

standoutFeatures.title: The entry Falcon2 Pro
standoutFeatures.body: At $899 for the single unit (Creality store, October 2026), the 22W is the least expensive way to get the Falcon2 Pro enclosure.
